content.text: What is current validation mechanism? Do not make any changes. just evaluation.
I’ll inspect the repository’s validation guidance and scripts, then assess how the checks work. I’ll keep this read-only.

The repo uses risk levels V0–V3 and a shared validation script for local runs and CI. I also found a candidate-specific 44-batch fallback for B3-2★. I’m checking which safeguards the script enforces and which depend on the operator.

The current mechanism combines **risk-based local checks, C# regression tests, Lean validation, and automatic CI**. I inspected the implementation and guidance; I made no changes and ran no builds or tests.

Local scope is selected by the agent from [AGENTS.md](/D:/Projects/katlangnet/AGENTS.md:195):

| Level | Required checks |
|---|---|
| V0 | Diff, whitespace and documentation consistency |
| V1 | Affected project build and directly related tests |
| V2 | Affected builds, neighboring suites and relevant parity/Lean checks |
| V3 | Full solution build, full C# suite and all seven Lean targets |

Parser, elaboration, ownership, binding, evaluator, optimizer, async, loading and other fundamental changes require V3. Classification is a human/agent responsibility; the script does not determine risk.

The canonical V3 command is:

```powershell
pwsh -NoProfile -File ./scripts/validate-all.ps1 -Phase All
```

[The script](/D:/Projects/katlangnet/scripts/validate-all.ps1:387) performs the full solution build, runs all three test projects with `--no-build`, checks whitespace, then builds seven Lean targets. Those cover semantic guards, arity laws, AST compatibility, the arity algebra and both differential corpora.

Important safeguards include:

- Before/after fingerprints of staged, unstaged and untracked content.
- Neutralization of inherited artifact-regeneration flags.
- Command/exit-code records, TRX results and allocation diagnostics.
- A separate **forced invocation-plan mode**, required for relevant META/need-binding changes.
- Local validation commands run sequentially against an unchanged candidate.

Lean/C# agreement is checked using generated Lean programs derived from the actual elaborated C# AST, with explicit exclusions and coverage checks. This provides **bounded differential evidence and proofs of selected laws**, not a proof of the entire evaluator. [Specification explanation](/D:/Projects/katlangnet/docs/design/executable-language-spec.md:296)

[CI](/D:/Projects/katlangnet/.github/workflows/validate.yml:1) runs ordinary .NET and Lean validation on every PR and push to `main`, using separate Ubuntu jobs. Diagnostics upload even after failure.

My assessment: the coverage design is strong, especially the semantic correspondence checks and preservation of the candidate. The main limitations are:

- **Completeness enforcement is weaker than the written policy.** The wrapper warns about missing TRXs; it does not independently reject zero-test execution, skipped cases or incomplete discovery. Its pass/fail primarily follows command exit codes. [Implementation](/D:/Projects/katlangnet/scripts/validate-all.ps1:204)
- **Forced-plan validation is not automatic in CI.** Running it when required depends on following the local instructions.
- **The B3-2★ batching exception is candidate-specific.** Its approved 44-batch procedure audits exact case coverage under 900-second/6-GiB limits, but cannot establish whole-process cross-class state, lifetime or contention behavior. Canonical whole-core completion remains recorded as incomplete. [Acceptance report](/D:/Projects/katlangnet/experimental/features/alias-unify-1-b32-final-corrections-2026-10-30.md:162)

This evaluates the mechanism; it does not establish a fresh validation pass for the current working tree.

content.text:
**Make V3 one ordinary full-suite run, with no elapsed-time cutoff.** Keep ordinary/planned comparisons inside dedicated tests.

I recommend these changes:

1. **Remove the mandatory second full-suite run.**  
   [AGENTS.md](/D:/Projects/katlangnet/AGENTS.md:228) currently explicitly requires forced-plan validation after ordinary validation for certain changes. Replace that requirement with one .NET suite execution and one build of each canonical Lean target. The current instruction is why the agent launches both modes.

2. **Remove timeout-based termination and fallback.**  
   The session’s [supervisor](/C:/Users/mikus/.codex/artifacts/b32-main-validation-20261030/phase-supervisor.py:26) kills the entire phase after 900 seconds. The orchestration then starts the 44-batch procedure, repeating work already attempted. Remove that automatic sequence. Continue waiting while recording progress; elapsed time should trigger a status report, not termination or a restart.

   The repository’s normal command already provides the basic sequence:
   ```powershell
   pwsh -NoProfile -File ./scripts/validate-all.ps1 -Phase All
   ```
   It has no internal phase timeout.

3. **Preserve plan-route coverage through focused tests within that single run.**  
   This is already partly implemented: [InvocationPlanTests](/D:/Projects/katlangnet/tests/KatLang.Tests/InvocationPlanTests.cs:594) compares ordinary and planned execution, including effects and accounting. [InvocationRouteCorpusTests](/D:/Projects/katlangnet/tests/KatLang.Tests/InvocationRoute/InvocationRouteCorpusTests.cs:84) also compares ordinary/planned pairs across engines.

   Audit those comparisons and the tests dependent on the process-wide forced flag. Cover any missing invariants using the existing per-run test seam. That avoids repeating unrelated parser, formatting, CLI and API tests.

4. **Make completion a hard acceptance condition.**  
   Require results from every expected test project, actual executed tests, and no unexplained missing or duplicate cases. The current wrapper’s TRX completeness checks are warning-only. A stopped or incomplete run must remain incomplete.

This deliberately exchanges **two complete execution-mode matrices** for **one complete suite plus focused mode-equivalence coverage**. It preserves the important comparisons while removing blanket duplication.

CI separately has configured 60-minute .NET and 30-minute Lean job limits; those also need review if your no-timeout requirement includes CI. [Workflow](/D:/Projects/katlangnet/.github/workflows/validate.yml:21)

No files or running processes were changed.

content.text:
**Yes—running the full suite in GitHub Actions is a reasonable approach**, provided focused checks run locally and CI must pass before merging. The main tradeoff is slower feedback on regressions outside the local selection.

The current repository policy explicitly requires local V3, so adopting this approach needs a deliberate update to [AGENTS.md](/D:/Projects/katlangnet/AGENTS.md:197).

I would use this workflow:

| Stage | Validation |
|---|---|
| During development | Affected build and directly relevant tests |
| Final PR candidate | Full .NET suite once, plus all seven Lean targets in CI |
| Before merge | Require both CI checks to pass for the final commit |

This avoids running the complete suite locally and then repeating it in CI. CI already invokes the canonical validation script; branch protection would need to enforce its results.

There are also concrete performance improvements worth investigating. The **completed portion** of the current run shows:

| Test class | Cases | Accumulated test duration |
|---|---:|---:|
| Structural-depth process tests | 14 | ~116 seconds |
| Budget cross-talk matrix | 47 | ~75 seconds |
| Async differential tests | 3,548 | ~26 seconds |

These are partial measurements, not a complete profile, and accumulated durations differ from overall elapsed time. They show why simply reducing test counts would be a poor first step.

My priority order would be:

1. **Eliminate repeated full-suite work.** Remove the forced whole-suite pass and timeout/restart/batching sequence discussed earlier. This saves work without making individual tests faster.

2. **Reduce subprocess harness overhead.** Several safety tests launch `dotnet vstest` against the large test assembly for individual probes. A small, prebuilt probe executable could reduce repeated runner startup and discovery while preserving a fresh process and the required stack/GC settings. [Current harness](/D:/Projects/katlangnet/tests/KatLang.Tests/AstStructuralDepthTests.cs:1707)

3. **Share safe test preparation.** Reuse immutable corpus construction and parsing where those operations are setup rather than the behavior being tested. Keep evaluator state and observations fresh. The budget matrix also repeats boundary discovery; that deserves profiling before attempting reuse. [Boundary search](/D:/Projects/katlangnet/tests/KatLang.Tests/BudgetCrossTalkMatrixTests.cs:597)

4. **Distribute CI work by measured duration.** Partition whole test collections across independent jobs, ensuring each case belongs to exactly one partition. Preserve collection fixtures and report complete coverage. GitHub supports matrix jobs for this. [GitHub documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-what-workflows-do/run-job-variations)

I would **not blindly increase parallelism**: xUnit already runs collections concurrently by default, and additional subprocesses can increase contention. [xUnit documentation](https://xunit.net/docs/running-tests-in-parallel)

The best first change is the validation workflow; the strongest test-code optimization candidate is the subprocess harness. No files or running processes were changed.
